subject: Post-call recap: AetherBio dedicated GPU on-ramp and isolation guardrails
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@aetherbio.ai>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@aetherbio.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: AetherBio dedicated GPU on-ramp and isolation guardrails

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and next steps so we have a single source of truth. Short version: we captured the operational constraints and a recommended on-ramp that lets you start small while preserving strict tenant isolation and the ability to scale during peak inference.

What we confirmed (pain points & goals)
- PHI + sensitive PII in inference payloads; primary requirement = tenant-level isolation + customer-managed KMS.
- Current peak traffic estimates: ~600 concurrent inference streams (avg 256 tokens) with expected 3x growth in 6 months.
- Latency target: P95 < 200ms for typical prompts, P99 target ~350ms (for 2k token windows) for realtime features.
- Cost sensitivity: want a predictable per-token budget and ability to cap burst spend.

Recommended reserved-capacity plan (high level)
- Phase 1 (on-ramp): Reserve 4xA100-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool with strict tenant isolation and no co-tenancy. Autoscale burst policy to +2 GPUs for brief spikes.
- Phase 2 (scale): Move to 8 GPUs committed when sustained throughput (qps) exceeds the 4-GPU runway. We recommend a time-based canary for rollouts.
- Runtime knobs: aggressive KV prefix caching enabled for stable prompts; quantization profile q4_0 for non-privacy-sensitive models to cut token cost ~30% where quality is acceptable.

SLA & operational asks
- Redwood target: 99.9% availability for the dedicated pool, 24/7 incident escalation, and SLA credits for sustained breaches (we'll include in draft).
- Recovery: RTO goal of 30 minutes for pool-level failures; RPO for logs >= 1 hour retention by default, longer retention available as an add-on.

Attachments we will send by EOD:
- aetherbio-sla-draft-v1.pdf (SLA + availability / incident process)
- mutual-action-plan.xlsx (milestones: SOC2 items, procurement dates, POC acceptance criteria)

Immediate next steps
- Redwood (Monica + Ben): share SLA draft and MAP by COB today.
- AetherBio (Sara): share procurement timeline (PO target date) and any hard gating items (legal/infosec windows).
- Align on a 30–45 minute technical handoff with your infra lead next week to walk config and VPN/KMS steps. Proposed slots: Thu 05/07 or Mon 05/11.

If I've missed anything or any of the bullets above are off, flag it and I'll update the MAP.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you on the dedicated pool.

--
Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Monica — thanks for the clear recap. This matches our notes. A couple of clarifications from our side before we sign off on the MAP: 

Top questions
1) Tenant isolation: we need guaranteed single-tenant lanes for model evaluation and production. Can the dedicated pool be configured so the evaluation nodes never touch production data?
2) KMS / key separation: we need customer-managed keys (we use AWS KMS) and proof that key material is never exported.
3) RTO/RPO: is the 30 min RTO a hard SLA or an operational target? We need clarity for procurement.
4) On-prem option: we are exploring an air-gapped variant for a subset of models. Is Redwood's private package compatible with our planned on-prem GPU hosts?

Procurement timeline (tentative)
- Legal review window: 3 weeks starting 05/10
- Budget approval: target PO by 06/01
- Infra handoff: target technical kick on 06/07

We'll review the SLA draft and MAP when you send. Also adding procurement@aetherbio.ai on this thread for visibility.

Thanks,
Sara

Sara / team — appreciate the quick turnaround and the timeline. Short answers inline and next steps below.

Answers to your questions
1) Tenant isolation: yes — we can provision a single-tenant lane for evaluation that never runs on the production pool. We'll include a clear separation in the MAP and the onboarding runbook.
2) KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed AWS KMS and HSM integrations. Keys remain in your KMS; Redwood will never have export rights. We'll add the KMS flow diagram to the MAP.
3) RTO/RPO: 30-minute RTO is the operational SLA target; the SLA draft includes credit terms for prolonged outages. We'll call out measurable RPO for logs and KV cache in the SLA appendix.
4) On-prem / private: Redwood Private is compatible with on-prem GPU hosts (we've done air-gapped deployments). We'll surface the minimal networking and hardware checklist in the MAP; full on-prem pricing is a separate engagement — we can include a high-level estimate in the next version.

What I'm attaching now
- aetherbio-sla-draft-v1.pdf (SLA summary + incident process + credit model)
- mutual-action-plan.xlsx (updated with KMS and evaluation lane tasks)

Proposed next meetings
- Technical handoff (infra + security): Thu 2026-05-07 10:00 PDT (30–45 min) — please confirm availability.
- Commercial check-in (procurement/legal): Tue 2026-05-12 11:00 PDT — roadmap and PO timing.

Action items (owners)
- AetherBio: confirm procurement PO target and legal constraints (procurement@aetherbio.ai) — owner: Tom (by 2026-05-10).

If that looks good I'll lock the calendar invites and share the Drive links.

Thanks — excited to get this moving.
